{{< include ../_includes/research-profile-en.md >}}

::: {.research-intro .lead}
I am a biostatistician working at the intersection of statistical methodology and clinical research. I study methods and effect measures that help researchers design studies and interpret their findings.
:::

::: {.research-topic}
## [01]{.topic-number aria-hidden="true"} Causal inference & observational studies

I am interested in how study design and confounding adjustment inform the estimation of exposure effects. My published work examines cohort and self-controlled case series designs for vaccine safety studies, as well as adjusted risk differences for rare events.

[Selected methodological work](#selected-publications){.arrow-link}
:::

::: {.research-topic}
## [02]{.topic-number aria-hidden="true"} Time-to-event outcomes

My interests include the analysis and interpretation of time-to-event data in clinical research. My teaching addresses practical questions about group comparisons, effect estimation, and the reporting of survival analyses.

[Public teaching record (Japanese, PDF)](https://cdn.kyodonewsprwire.jp/prwfile/release/M106906/202404260076/_prw_PR1fl_cDK0Xn4i.pdf){.arrow-link}
:::

::: {.research-topic}
## [03]{.topic-number aria-hidden="true"} Statistical methods for clinical research

I collaborate on clinical trials and observational studies, from study design to analysis and interpretation. A recurring focus in my methodological work is the performance of statistical measures under conditions encountered in practice, including sparse outcomes in large datasets.

[Publications and collaborations](publications.qmd){.arrow-link}
:::
